title: Emit Coons-patch DSL from quad-layout T-mesh patches
description:
Surfaced during PATCH-42 housekeeping audit. End goal of the PATCH-37 quad-layout pipeline is to produce procedural-mesh DSL (.dsl files in src/main/resources/dsl/) that the existing CoonsPatchNode + node graph runtime can ingest. This is the artifact that closes the 'mesh decomposition -> procedural reconstruction' loop.

What we have:
- CoonsPatchNode + supporting Coons primitives in geometry/mesh/nodes/patch/
- DSL parser + node graph runtime that consumes coons_patch(...) calls
- TMesh patches with 4-arc cyclic ordering and per-arc parametric length
- Quantization gives integer dimensions per arc

What's missing:
- QuadLayoutDslEmitter: walks each TPatch, fits a curve representation to each of the 4 arcs (Bezier or polyline), emits coons_patch DSL
- Per-arc curve fitting from face-crossings + parametric length
- Whole-mesh DSL assembly with shared boundary curves between adjacent patches (so reconstruction is watertight)

Blockers:
- 0 TPatches on Hand-30k currently (IGM convergence + T-junction enumeration -- see PATCH-Q8 ticket about scene integration for the same blocker)
- Need a way to express the per-arc curve compactly enough that the DSL stays human-readable

Out of scope:
- Upstream IGM convergence work
- Multi-patch quad meshes from QEx (PATCH-43 produces those; this ticket emits LAYOUT-level DSL)
- Animation / parametric variation of the emitted DSL (that's a future enhancement)

SCOPE (user, 2026-10-02): this ticket replaces CRAW-4 as the saved quad layout. The goal is to throw away the underlying model and rebuild the quad layout from the .dsl alone. The saved file must not `load_mesh` a source or carrier mesh, must not reference any .off, .obj or other mesh file, and must not use any absolute path. No caching is wanted.

CRAW-4 went the other way: it saved a 13853-quad carrier .off and re-attached the layout with `network_node`, `network_arc` and `via1..via32` waypoints snapped to that carrier. That approach is dropped. Do not build on `QuadLayoutDslWriter`'s carrier or via scheme. Reusing pieces of its sorting or byte-stable emission is fine.

Starting point: fertility now produces 284 patches through the quad-layout scene, so the old "0 TPatches" blocker is gone. Emit one `coons_patch` per layout patch. Each boundary curve is fitted once and shared by the two patches on either side, so the result is watertight by construction. Patch identity must survive a reload, because CRAW-6 attaches labels to these patches and CRAW-19 builds on them.

FIDELITY RULING (user, 2026-10-02): the first pass's Coons interior error is not acceptable (mean 0.367, max 5.6 on a 256.7 diagonal; the live quad grid gives 0.028 / 0.956). The fix is to SPLIT patches until each meets a tolerance, keeping the result a valid quad layout. Splits must add NO T-junctions:
- A split cuts a patch along one row or column line of its quad grid, running between two opposite sides.
- Where that line meets a neighbouring patch, the cut carries on across the neighbour, along the same quad-grid line, out through the neighbour's opposite side. It keeps going patch to patch, like a loop cut along a chord of the layout, until it closes on itself or reaches a mesh boundary.
- Every new endpoint is therefore a proper node on both sides. A cut is never left ending in the middle of a side.
- The extracted quad grid is conforming, so these lines always exist and the cut polylines are exact quad-edge chains.
- Existing T-junctions in the layout, where a side is made of several arcs, are left as they are; no new ones are created.

Choosing splits: greedy. Measure each patch's Coons-versus-original error, cut the worst patch through the middle of its longer direction, re-measure, and repeat until every patch meets the tolerance. The tolerance is a parameter of the save command, as a fraction of the bounding-box diagonal. Report the full curve of patch count against max/mean error for fertility, so the user can pick the default.

Patch identity: splitting must be deterministic and byte-stable. A patch that is cut gets child names derived from the parent (for example patch_12 becomes patch_12_0 and patch_12_1), so labels attached to an unsplit patch keep working.

CUT RULE (user, 2026-10-02): replace "cut the worst patch through the middle of its longer direction". The midpoint ignores both the shape and where the error is: at the neck between the baby's and the mother's heads on fertility, no cut lands at the waist, and some midpoint loops slice ~600 patches at once.

New rule, still greedy and deterministic:
- Pick the worst patch over tolerance, as now.
- For every interior grid line of that patch, in both directions, trace the conforming loop the cut would make, exactly as the propagation does now, without applying it. A line running around a narrow neck closes after a few patches; a line running the length of the model slices hundreds.
- Score each candidate loop as the error it removes divided by the number of patches it slices. The error removed is the sum, over the sliced patches, of the error before the cut minus the worse of the two halves' errors after it. Take the best loop. Break ties by patch index, then direction, then line index, so the output stays byte-stable.
- If scoring every line is too slow on fertility, measure the halves' error on a subsample, or score only every k-th line and then refine around the best one. Report the save time either way.

Report the same patch-count vs max/mean error curve as before, side by side with the midpoint rule's (0.004 -> 1167 patches, max 0.99; 0.005 -> 985, max 1.27), plus a screenshot of the neck between the two heads.

BEST-LOOP RESULT (2026-10-02): CoonsLayoutSplitter now scores every interior grid line of the worst patch, both directions, by tracing the conforming loop the cut would make (read-only, against an arc->walking-sides index) and scoring it as error removed / patches added. The denominator counts a patch crossed by both a column and a row line of the same loop as the extra pieces it really becomes, so the traced count equals the real cut count on all 314 fertility cuts checked. Half errors are measured exactly (equal to patchError after the real cut) and cached per patch until it is cut. Ties go to column lines, then the lower line. No subsampling was needed. At the default: 993 patches (-15%), .dsl 580852 bytes (-13%), 0 T-junctions, closed, euler -6, re-save byte-identical, saved fertility_coons_layout.dsl regenerated. The mean error is higher at the same max (0.075 vs 0.064) because the rule optimises the worst patch and adds fewer patches. One long loop is still forced: at 0.009 the best line of the worst patch adds 518 patches (306 -> 841), because every line of that patch runs the length of the model. Neck between the heads: the midpoint layout cuts on either side of the waist and leaves the narrowest point inside a patch, while best-loop puts a cut line through the waist (tmp/patch57_neck_{bestloop,midpoint,unsplit}.png and *_top_*.png). Unit test CoonsLayoutSplitterTest: the T-junction assertion now checks that no T-junction is new (best-loop no longer happens to cut through the fixture's junction), plus a new strip test where the midpoint rule would slice all four patches and best-loop closes its cuts inside the bumpy ones. Suite 335/335.

T-JUNCTION EXPERIMENT (user, 2026-10-03): try allowing T-junctions. This overrides the "NO T-junctions" part of the fidelity ruling for this experiment.

- A cut slices only the patch being cut, along one of its grid lines between two opposite sides. It is no longer carried through the neighbours.
- Where a cut ends partway along a side shared with a neighbour, split that shared arc at the joint (ensureJoint already does this), so the neighbour's side walks two arcs. The neighbour keeps its grid and Coons boundary unchanged, so the surface stays watertight. Because cuts follow grid lines of a conforming grid, the quad grid itself stays conforming; only the patch layout gains T-junctions, the same kind the layout already has.
- Choosing the cut: pick the worst patch, then try every interior grid line in both directions and take the one whose worse half has the lowest error. Break ties by direction, then line index, for byte-stable output.
- Keep the conforming best-loop rule's numbers from the previous section for comparison. Report the same curve (patches, max/mean, .dsl size, split time), the number of T-junctions added, and a screenshot of the neck between the two heads.

T-JUNCTION RESULT (2026-10-03): CoonsLayoutSplitter now cuts only the worst patch, along the grid line (either direction) whose worse half has the lowest error, ties to column lines then the lower line; a cut end inside a shared side splits that arc (ensureJoint) so the neighbour walks two arcs with its grid and Coons boundary unchanged. Loop tracing and the joint drain are gone. definition-of-done:
1. A save command in the quad-layout scene writes a self-contained .dsl after the full pipeline. The file contains no load_mesh, no mesh-file reference and no absolute path. Proof: delete the source and any intermediate mesh files, then load the .dsl.
2. On fertility, the unsplit layout reloads with the 254 patches current master produces (replacing the stale 284) and the same patch adjacency (which patch borders which, along which arc), and the saved layout is watertight: shared boundaries are emitted once and referenced by both patches, with no cracks.
3. Geometric fidelity is reported: the max and mean distance from the reconstructed surface to the original fertility mesh, as numbers in the final report and on the ticket. The user rules on whether the curve representation is good enough.
4. Patch identity is stable across a save, reload and re-save cycle: patch order and naming are byte-identical, so labels added later (CRAW-6) stay attached.
5. The reload runs no solver stage: no cross-field, seamless, motorcycle, quantization, embedding, grid-map or Newton stage.
6. Writer output is byte-stable across two runs.
7. A launch.json entry loads the saved fertility .dsl. Before and after screenshots under tmp/ compare the live pipeline render with the reload.
8. Build checkstyle-green. Round-trip unit test on a small synthetic layout (plane or torus fixtures).
9. The fidelity and round-trip numbers come from test/benchmark/CoonsLayoutRoundTripBenchmark (run with -Dtest=), whose '[coons-layout]' summary log lines (counts/adjacency/watertightness/reload time, the max/mean distance to the original mesh, and the '[coons-layout] tolerance' sweep lines giving the error-versus-patch-count curve) are the acceptance numbers and stay. Keeps the benchmark log line '[coons-layout] distance to original (bbox diagonal ...)': it is the DoD 3 fidelity number.
10. Fidelity by conforming splits: on fertility, after saving at the chosen tolerance (a parameter of the save command, a fraction of the bounding-box diagonal), the reloaded surface's max distance to the original is within tolerance. The reloaded layout has no T-junctions beyond those already in the pipeline's layout: every split endpoint is a node on both adjacent patches. Split patches are named after their parent (patch_12_0, patch_12_1). The error-versus-patch-count curve is reported.

Keeps '[coons-layout] tolerance none': the unsplit row of the error-versus-patch-count curve.

3. Save, reload and re-save, then byte-compare the two files.

Conforming splits (CoonsLayoutSplitter, nodes/patch): greedy worst-patch-first; a patch is cut along the grid row/column line through the middle of its longer direction (by quad count), the line's points are the extracted grid's exact quad-edge chain; each cut endpoint is made an arc joint (splitting the arc in every patch that walks it) and queued; any patch still holding that joint inside one of its sides is cut along the same grid line out through its opposite side, repeating until the chord closes, reaches the boundary, or lands on an existing node where the neighbours already have corners. Error per patch = max distance of its Coons grid points and quad centres to the original mesh (TriangleBvh.fromMesh). Children named parent_0/parent_1 (left/bottom first), arcs renumbered by first use, layout_patch gained a name= input. Save command: 'sl <path.dsl> [tolerance]', default 0.004 of the bbox diagonal.
